title: Polynomial Division and the Remainder Theorem
seo_title: Polynomial Long and Synthetic Division Worksheet, Remainder Theorem (Algebra 2) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x − a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x − a) is a factor of p(x).
meta_desc: Free Algebra 2 worksheet on polynomial division: long division, synthetic division, the Remainder Theorem, the Factor Theorem and factoring completely. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The remainder when P(x) is divided by (x − a) is P(a).
key_sub: (x − a) is a factor exactly when P(a) = 0.
body_html:
How it works

Long division works like number division: divide the first terms, multiply, subtract, bring down, and repeat.

Synthetic division is a shortcut for dividing by (x − a). Put a in the box, write the coefficients (0 for any missing term), bring down the first one, multiply by a, add, and repeat. The last number is the remainder.

  • Remainder Theorem: dividing P(x) by (x − a) leaves remainder P(a).
  • Factor Theorem: (x − a) is a factor exactly when P(a) = 0.
Example

Divide x³ − 2x² − 5x + 6 by (x − 3).

Box: 3. Coefficients 1, −2, −5, 6

Bottom row: 1, 1, −2, 0

Answer: x² + x − 2, remainder 0

Example

Is (x + 2) a factor of x³ + 8?

P(−2) = −8 + 8 = 0

Answer: Yes

Common mistakes

  • Putting −3 in the box for (x − 3). Use the zero of the divisor: 3.
  • Leaving out a missing term. Write 0 for it, or the columns shift.
  • Subtracting wrongly in long division. Subtract the whole product: change every sign.
  • Checking P(−a) instead of P(a) for the factor (x − a).

faq.a: When a polynomial P(x) is divided by (x − a), the remainder is P(a).
(x − a) is a factor of P(x) exactly when P(a) = 0.

faq.q: When can you use synthetic division?
faq.a: When you divide by a linear factor of the form x − a. For x + 3, use −3 in the box.

faq.q: Why do you need a zero placeholder?
faq.a: Each column stands for one power of x. A missing term must be written as 0 so the other coefficients stay in the right columns.
